verdict.rationale: Vast.ai documents interruptible instances as a first-party instance type. They use a bidding system, are often 50%+ cheaper than on-demand, and sit in a low-priority tier that "may be paused", so the discounted-capacity part of the story is clearly delivered. The preemption semantics, however, amount to that short note plus the priority-level framing, which falls short of "clearly documented". Missing for 10: detailed preemption semantics (what triggers a pause, how being outbid works, any notice period, what happens to running state or data, resume behavior) and independent or hands-on corroboration of interruptible behavior.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can rent spot or interruptible GPU capacity at a deep discount with clearly documented preemption semantics

citations.quote: Interruptible instances use a bidding system: Lowest cost (often 50%+ cheaper than on-demand)
Interruptible: Low Priority. Lowest cost, may be paused
Vast.ai offers three instance types with different priority levels and pricing models to match your workload requirements and budget.
